issue.title: Give the artifact store a lifecycle - report, dry-run pruning, and opt-in retention
issue.description: The artifact-file store can be measured, drained, and bounded: `sase artifact stats` reports its economics, `sase artifact prune` and `sase artifact reclaim` are dry-run by default and route every removal through a restorable trash, an opt-in `artifacts.retention` policy keeps the store bounded going forward, and nothing an agent declared or a bead, plan, or ChangeSpec references is ever removed.

issue.title: Rust core: store economics, retention planner, and trash primitives
issue.description: core-lifecycle: add a pure store-economics aggregator, a pure retention planner, and clock-free trash store/list/restore/purge primitives to `sase_core`, expose all four through `sase_core_rs`, and release the crate.

issue.title: Store economics report and the protected-reference scan
issue.description: py-report: raise the `sase-core-rs` pin, add the Python bridges for economics and retention planning, add the bead/plan/ChangeSpec reference scan that produces protected artifact ids, and ship `sase artifact stats` as a read-only report with a JSON mode.

issue.title: Dry-run-first pruning and the trash lifecycle
issue.description: py-prune: add `sase artifact prune` (dry run unless `--apply`) and the `sase artifact trash {list,purge,restore}` group, with index-row removal and restoration performed under the existing index lock and every removal routed through the trash.

issue.title: Retroactive version-control reclaim of the pooled bytes
issue.description: py-reclaim: add `sase artifact reclaim`, which converts stored automatic rows whose exact content is reproducible from a durable ref into byte-free VCS-backed rows and trashes the redundant copies, reusing the capture policy's git probe and verifying by digest first.

issue.title: Opt-in retention configuration and enforcement
issue.description: retention-config: add the `artifacts.retention` configuration block defaulting to disabled, its schema entries and accessors, and the bounded, fail-safe enforcement pass that runs after automatic capture at finalization and purges expired trash.

issue.title: Documentation, skill, and configuration reference
issue.description: docs-and-skill: document the store lifecycle, the new subcommands, the trash contract, and the retention block across the CLI, configuration, and artifact docs, and refresh the `sase_artifact_file` skill source and its deployed copy.

payload.entry: docs-and-skill phase complete. docs/cli.md: retargeted the prune/reclaim/stats/trash rows at a new Store Lifecycle anchor (the old #artifact-consumption-ledger anchor did not exist) and added prose for the staged report -> dry-run -> trash contract. docs/configuration.md: documented the artifacts.retention block (yaml + field table with types/defaults/minimums), its fail-open reads, the finalization summary/skip lines, and how the same values drive prune/stats/trash purge; cross-linked artifacts.capture to the lifecycle section; expanded the sase artifact flag table with per-subcommand trash list/purge/restore rows, added the missing create -b/--bead flag, and added a trash-layout paragraph. docs/agent_images.md: new Store Lifecycle section covering the stage table, the six-rule protection contract, stats, the reclaim workflow including why a reclaimed row's id changes and a reason-by-reason table for unresolved rows (verified against _ineligible_reason/_resolve_candidate), prune, the trash layout and grace period, and opt-in enforcement. Skill source src/sase/xprompts/skills/sase_artifact_file.md: new Retention section telling agents that declared artifacts are permanent, automatic captures are not, that a file: ref persisted in a bead/plan/ChangeSpec or consumed via @file: is thereby protected, that reclaim changes ids, and not to run --apply/purge unasked. Parser: sharpened prune -b/--before (DATE grammar) and trash purge (irreversibility + grace-period source) help. Verified: just fmt, just check green through lint (ruff/mypy/keep-sorted/symvision/toobig/changelog/markdown) and just test 24496 passed / 7 skipped. Every doc claim was checked against the implementation (prune -g defaults to artifacts.retention.keep_per_label but -b has no config default; reclaim -d defaults to 100; only reclaim --apply prints the disk-not-freed warning). NOT DONE and blocking one check: sase init skills --check still reports the 5 provider SKILL.md files as needing overwrite. Per the generated_skills memory a chezmoi deploy is refused from a dirty/unlanded tree, so the deploy must run as 'sase skill init --force' after this commit lands on master.

Verified all six phases against source, not just reports. sase-ba.1: economics.rs/retention.rs/trash.rs exist in sase-core beside vcs.rs, ARTIFACT_FILE_LIFECYCLE_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1, all six PyO3 bindings plus the schema accessor registered and importable, 'sase core health' passes. sase-ba.2-.4: exercised read-only against the real store - stats reports 4076 automatic candidates / 226 explicit + 4 referenced protected / 0 unavailable sources; 'prune -g 3' and 'reclaim -l 200' are dry-run and correctly bucket explicit (226) and referenced (1) as untouched; trash empty; doctor healthy. sase-ba.5: artifacts.retention block, schema entries, four accessors and the fail-safe finalization pass are present with the planned test cases plus a consumed-row case; the plan's temporary DEFAULT_* constants were correctly dropped for the accessors. sase-ba.6: docs land in cli.md, configuration.md and a new agent_images.md Store Lifecycle section.

Integration (step 2) found and fixed two real gaps from work that landed alongside the epic: (1) sase-bb added durable artifact references to beads after this epic's protection scan was written; bead refs live in the sidecar's issues.jsonl and events/streams/*.jsonl, and .jsonl was not a scanned suffix, so a 'sase bead ref add' reference was unprotected until the next page publication - added .jsonl to the scan (+0.26s on a 5.4s real scan) with a regression test and a docs precision fix. (2) 'sase artifact create -b/--bead' shipped in 87ece3ee3 but its documentation only reached the deployed chezmoi skill copies and existed in no sase commit, so regenerating from this epic's skill source would have silently deleted it; restored it to the source ('sase skill init --diff' artifact-file diff went from +29 -14 to +29 -1). just check is green through every fmt and lint stage including symvision and toobig; committed-plan validation passes and the artifact/skill/docs test suites pass.
